verses.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
verses.2: A man who is in a state of impurity or sinfulness should go to the priest or one of his sons.
verses.3: And the priest saw that the sore area on his skin had turned white. The appearance of the sore area became more severe as it grew larger. The priest saw this and became disgusted by it.
verses.4: And if it is a female bird, then it is in its nest. There’s no sight of anything from outside the nest. Its feathers haven’t turned white yet. The priest will mark the spot where the bird was touched for seven days.
verses.5: And on the seventh day, the priest saw that the mark was still there in his eyes. He did not remove the mark from his eyes. The priest kept it there for seven days.
verses.6: And on the seventh day, the priest saw him again. He saw that the mark had disappeared from his body. The priest then washed him with water and made him clean.
verses.7: And if he were to remove the covering from it after seeing it, in order to purify himself. Then, once again, he should go to the priest.
verses.8: And the priest saw that the scapegoat was torn in pieces in the sanctuary; and the priest smeared the blood on the altar.
verses.9: It is harmful when it occurs in a person; then it must be brought before the priest.
verses.10: And the priest saw that the tent was turned white. It became a white tent, and from its fabric came life.
verses.11: A filthy smell is present in his breath. And the priest’s impurity cannot be covered up, for he is indeed impure.
verses.12: And if the worm blooms in the garden, and covers every corner of the garden from its head to its feet, then all those places will be visible to the eyes of the priest.
verses.13: And the priest saw that the disease had covered all of his body. But he was healed; his skin became pure and white again.
verses.14: And on the day that it was seen, living flesh was created.
verses.15: And the priest saw that the blood was still alive. But when he covered it with a cloth, the blood became impure. It became a source of infection.
verses.16: For the living creature will return to its original state, become white again, and come before the priest.
verses.17: And the priest saw that the mark had turned white. Then the priest purified the mark, making it clean again.
verses.18: And in the flesh, when it becomes rotten and decomposes, it will die.
verses.19: And it shall be in the place where the “shachin” is placed, or in the place where the “bananah” occurs. It will be visible to the priest.
verses.20: And the priest saw that there was a lowly appearance from among the trees. Its branches became white, and the priest touched them with his hand. It was a beautiful sight indeed.
verses.21: And if the priest sees that there is no white door in it, and that it isn’t low, then it isn’t acceptable. The priest must cover it for seven days.
verses.22: And if you touch it in the wilderness, and the priest examines it and finds it to be unclean, then it is unclean.
verses.23: And if the mountain stands in place, then the cloud will not be torn apart by the wind. And the priest will be purified.
verses.24: Or, it could be like a plant that grows from the ashes of fire. It would be like a plant that grows from the remains of the fire itself. It would be like a plant that grows from the ashes of destruction.
verses.25: And the priest saw that it had turned into a white hair in the darkness. It seemed to be a thorny plant. The priest touched it, and it became thorny again.
verses.26: And if the priest sees that there is no white door in the temple, and that there is no light from it, then he shall cover it for seven days.
verses.27: And on the seventh day, the priest saw that it was indeed a worm. The priest touched it, and it became infected with worms.
verses.28: And if the altar stands upright, without being tilted to one side, then it is like the handle of a hammer. And the priest will shine light upon it, just as if it were a hammer that has been sharpened.
verses.29: And neither man nor woman shall be touched in their head or in their genitals.
verses.30: And the priest saw the wound. It appeared to be a deep wound, with a thin, dirty yellowish hair covering it. The priest realized that it was probably a wound on the head or the elderly part of the body.
verses.31: And when the priest sees the mark of the scabies, and there is no visible sign of it on the skin; and if there isn’t any black hair there either, then the priest shall cover the mark of the scabies for seven days.
verses.32: And the priest saw that the mark had not healed on the seventh day. There was no yellowish discoloration on it, and the appearance of the mark was not severe at all.
verses.33: And he shall not remove the lampstand from its place. The priest shall keep it in secret for seven days.
verses.34: And the priest saw that the mark had not disappeared on the seventh day. It still remained visible in the air. The priest purified it by putting on his clothes and then cleaning it.
verses.35: And if he destroys the altar after his purification.
verses.36: And the priest saw that the seal was broken in the temple. The priest did not enter the holy door at all. It was a dishonest person.
verses.37: And if, in his eyes, there is a mark and a black hair on it, then the mark is healed. It becomes pure, and the priest is also purified.
verses.38: And neither man nor woman shall be in the wilderness, in the wilderness of their journeying.
verses.39: And the priest saw that in their midst there were flowers, like blossoms. They bloomed in a pure and holy place.
verses.40: And anyone who loses his head will be considered unclean.
verses.41: And if a hair falls from his face, he is considered unclean. He is considered impure.
verses.42: And when it is in a state of dryness or desolation, it becomes white and barren. It loses its beauty; it becomes like a barren plant.
verses.43: And the priest saw that the scribe had written something on his forehead or on his back, in a manner that resembled a mark of a worm on the skin.
verses.44: A wicked man is a lecherous person. He’s a man who contaminates others. The priest, in his own mind, touches him.
verses.45: And the wound on its skin will become boils; its head will become swollen. And on its mouth, it will be covered with dirt and filth. It will be called “dirty” or “filthy”.
verses.46: Every time someone touches it, the person who touches it becomes unclean. They sit alone outside the camp.
verses.47: And the garment should not be made of cloth that is infested with lice or worms. It should also not be made of silk or other delicate fabrics.
verses.48: In the morning, or in the evening, for planting and harvesting. Or in any other time of day.
verses.49: And the affected area would become greenish or brownish in color. It could also be covered with sores or ulcers. In any case, the affected area would become covered with sores. Then he would see the doctor.
verses.50: And the priest saw the sore, and he healed it after seven days.
verses.51: And he saw the mark on the seventh day, as if the mark had been made on the garment, or on the skin, or in any other part of the body. This mark was caused by the curse of God. It was a sign that someone had been afflicted with a curse from God.
verses.52: And he should burn the garment, or the rope, or the fabric itself. He should also burn all kinds of objects that might be contaminated by the poison; it must be burned with fire.
verses.53: And if the priest sees that the part of the garment that was touched has not been washed, either in the morning or in the evening, or at any other time of day.
verses.54: And the priest commanded that those who were affected with the disease be confined in a place where they could not move around. They were to be kept there for seven days.
verses.55: And the priest saw that after the plague had been applied, it did not change the condition of the wound. The wound remained unchanged. It was like fire that burned us; it destroyed everything. It either destroyed the skin or the flesh itself.
verses.56: And if the priest sees that the wound has healed after being bandaged, or if it has been torn off from the cloth, or from the bandage, or from the cloth used to cover it.
verses.57: And if you still see it on the leaves, or in the flowers, or anywhere else where it blooms, then it will be burned by fire. It will destroy whatever is covered with it.
verses.58: And the dirt, or the filth, or whatever that is that gets covered up and then becomes contaminated again. It’s then washed away once more, and purified.
verses.59: This is the law regarding how to clean or disinfect garments, or any other items that need to be cleaned. It also applies to all kinds of items that need to be purified or sealed.
